questions.question: What is the core freshness invariant for an admitted live-video frame?
options: It produces a decision within the deadline or follows an explicit drop, defer, or fallback policy
It must always wait in an unbounded FIFO queue
It must use the largest available model
It must be retained forever
questions.explanation: A bounded, explicit outcome prevents overload from silently turning current observations into stale decisions.

questions.question: A service admits 120 streams at 8 sampled frames per second. What is the incoming frame rate before complexity adjustments?
options: 15 frames/s
128 frames/s
960 frames/s
7,680 frames/s
questions.explanation: Incoming rate is streams multiplied by sampled FPS: 120 x 8 = 960 frames/s.

questions.question: Why should capacity be recalculated after losing a serving zone?
options: The model accuracy automatically becomes zero
The same demand now runs on fewer live replicas, increasing utilization and queue delay
Camera resolution always doubles
Non-max suppression stops using IoU
questions.explanation: Failure removes throughput while demand remains, so headroom and tail latency can fail even if steady state was healthy.

questions.question: What usually happens when a detection threshold is raised?
options: Recall and review load both always increase
Review load usually falls while false negatives can increase
Preprocessing becomes versioned automatically
GPU memory becomes unlimited
questions.explanation: A higher threshold accepts fewer candidates, which reduces alerts but can hide true events below the cutoff.

questions.question: Why is non-max suppression commonly class-aware?
options: Overlapping boxes from different classes may represent distinct hypotheses and should not suppress each other by default
IoU can only be computed for one class
Class-aware NMS removes every low-confidence box
It eliminates the need for a confidence threshold
questions.explanation: Duplicate suppression typically compares boxes within the same class so spatial overlap alone does not erase another class hypothesis.

questions.question: GPU inference p95 is low, but capture-to-decision p95 is high. What is the next useful investigation?
options: Profile decode, preprocessing, queue age, transfers, post-processing, tracking, and network time
Measure only parameter count
Increase queue length without a limit
Remove frame timestamps
questions.explanation: End-to-end latency includes every stage; queueing or CPU-side work can dominate a fast inference kernel.

questions.question: A candidate improves aggregate precision but low-light recall falls below the release floor. What is the defensible decision?
options: Release globally because the aggregate metric improved
Hold or narrow the release, investigate the slice, and preserve a rollback path
Delete the low-light slice
Raise the threshold without measuring consequences
questions.explanation: Named critical slices are release constraints; aggregate gains do not override a failed safety or product contract.
